title: Model-based estimation of leaf area in ozone-indicator tobacco plants
author: Agathokleous, Zhang, et al.

steps.title: Sow seeds and initial potting
steps.instruction: Sow Bel‑W3 tobacco seeds on 25 February in a pot containing Florabella soil (Klasmann‑Deilmann GmbH, Germany) and keep at room temperature; irrigate as needed to keep the substrate wet.

steps.title: Transfer seedlings to growth chamber
steps.instruction: Four days after sowing, move the pot to a closed growth chamber set to a 14 h light / 10 h dark photoperiod.

steps.title: Transplant to larger pots
steps.instruction: On 24 March, transplant each of the 350 seedlings into an individual 500 mL (500‑cc) pot filled with the same Florabella soil; on 27 March, select 120 uniform seedlings and place them in a semi‑open penthouse for acclimation to outdoor conditions.

steps.title: Daily midday shading
steps.instruction: From 30 March onward, move the plants under shade each midday until they are transplanted to the experimental field.

steps.title: Transplant to experimental plot
steps.instruction: On 3 May, transplant the seedlings from the pots into the ground of the experimental plot as illustrated in Fig. 1.

steps.title: Apply high‑NPK fertilizer
steps.instruction: Immediately after transplantation, fertilize with MAXIGRO 20‑20‑20 (Fertifarm Chemical Co., Cyprus) at the manufacturer’s rate of 5 kg acre⁻¹ (20 % N: 5.7 % nitrate, 3.9 % ammoniacal, 10.4 % urea; 20 % P₂O₅; 20 % K₂O).

steps.title: Control aphid outbreak
steps.instruction: On 15 May, spray plants with an insecticidal solution made of 5 mL commercial dish‑soap and 30 mL alcohol diluted in 1 L water; repeat if aphids persist.

steps.title: Prepare chemical treatment solutions
steps.instruction: On 21 May, prepare three foliar sprays: (1) distilled water (control); (2) ethylenediurea (EDU) at 500 ppm; (3) Vapor Gard (Intrachem Bio Italia, Cesena, IT) at 1 %, 5 % and 10 % (v/v) using the commercial product that contains 96 % di‑1‑p‑menthene and 4 % inert ingredients.

steps.title: Apply chemical treatments
steps.instruction: Randomly allocate plants to the three treatments and spray by hand until runoff; note that toxicity appears one day after spraying at 10 % and 5 % Vapor Gard but not at 1 %.

steps.title: Maintain irrigation and weed control
steps.instruction: Irrigate regularly throughout the field experiment to keep the soil moisturized; manually remove weeds on 30 May and 5 July.

steps.title: Collect leaves for measurement
steps.instruction: Sixty‑one days after transplanting, excise 138 leaves (excluding the most basal senescent leaves) from 40 randomly selected plants using scissors.

steps.title: Measure leaf length and width
steps.instruction: Measure each leaf’s length (distance from lowest to highest point) and maximum width (widest vertical distance) with a ruler accurate to 1 mm.

steps.title: Photograph leaves for image analysis
steps.instruction: Place each leaf next to a ruler, photograph from a fixed position with a digital camera, then import images into Adobe Photoshop CS4 Extended v.11.

steps.title: Process images and calculate area
steps.instruction: Convert each photo to Gray Scale, set the measurement scale to centimeters using the ruler in the image, and measure leaf area with Photoshop’s measurement tools.

steps.title: Compute width‑times‑length product
steps.instruction: For each leaf, calculate Width × Length (both in cm) and record the value alongside the measured area.

steps.title: Develop predictive regression model
steps.instruction: Plot Width × Length (independent variable) on the x‑axis against measured leaf area (dependent variable) on the y‑axis; fit a simple linear regression (y = β₁x + β₀) using statistical software, obtaining parameters (e.g., β₁ ≈ 0.6402, r = 0.928).

steps.title: Validate and improve model
steps.instruction: Apply the regression to the Width × Length data from a previous chamber experiment, compare predicted versus actual areas, and, if needed, integrate both datasets to obtain an improved model (e.g., r = 0.981, β₁ ≈ 0.657).
